thread.title: Stocks Rally On Election Results: Caterpillar Boosts Dow| Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Rally On Election Results: Caterpillar Boosts Dow| Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks opened sharply higher Wednesday, as election results largely met expectations and as investors turned their attention to the Federal Reserve's rate policy.
X Caterpillar ( CAT ) and UnitedHealth Group ( UNH ) jockeyed for the lead among Dow stocks. Amazon.com ( AMZN ) grabbed an early lead among rising FANG tech stocks. Earnings results sent Twilio ( TWLO ) and Etsy ( ETSY ) to steep early gains, while Zillow ( Z ), Infinera ( INFN ) and Innogen ( INGN ) dived.
The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite leapt 1% apiece at the starting bell. China's NetEase ( NTES ) and Wynn Resorts ( WYNN ) ran at the head of the Nasdaq. Davita Healthcare ( DVA ) and Cimarex Energy ( XEC ) rose to the S&P 500's largest early gains on election and earnings results.
The Dow Jones industrial average opened to a 0.9% gain. UnitedHealth surged 3.7%, Caterpillar advanced 1.7% in opening trade.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Election Results: Possible Positive For Market The stock market wasted no time in reacting to early election results, which pointed to Republicans strengthening their hold on the Senate, while Democrats flipped control of the House by a wide margin. A divided Congress raises concerns over gridlock and legislative stalemate in Washington. From the market's point of view, over the past 60 years, the S&P 500 has generally performed better during periods of a divided Congress , vs. periods when one party held both the House and the Senate.
Europe's markets rallied, with the CAC-40 in Paris rising 1.2%, Frankfurt's DAX up 1% and the FTSE 100 in London riding 1.1% higher in afternoon trade.
Asia markets were mixed, and closed as U.S. election results continued to roll in. China's benchmark indexes were mixed, with Hong Kong's Hang Seng up 0.1% and the Shanghai composite posting a 0.7% loss. In Japan, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 slipped 0.3% as it continues to meet resistance at its 50-day moving average.
Noble, Davita Jump On Election Results Among stocks showing the largest reaction to election results, Davita Healthcare Partners bolted 10% higher after Californians rejected Proposition 8, which would have limited revenue earned by dialysis clinics within the state. The Union-backed measure broke campaign spending records in California, according to the San Jose Mercury News . The measure would have required refunds from dialysis clinics of up to $100,000 to insurance providers and patients who paid out of pocket.
UnitedHealthcare surged, as analyst generally saw a divided Congress as a positive for Medicaid HMOs, hospitals stocks and others within the Affordable Care Act supply chain. The gain sent United to a new high, up about 9% since clearing a cup base in June.
Noble Energy jumped 4.4% after Raymond James upgraded the stock to outperform, from market perform. The note said the rejection by voters of Proposition 112 in Colorado removed overhanging uncertainty from the stock. Prop 112 would have required a setback of 2,500 feet for drilling operations near occupied buildings and some other facilities. Noble shares are attempting to climb off lows in a deep, four-month consolidation.
Anadarko Petroleum sparked 7% higher in early trade, also boosted by the Prop 112 vote.
Fed Meeting Begins The Federal Open Market Committee kicks off its two-day meeting Wednesday, delayed one day due to the election. A rate policy announcement is scheduled for Thursday afternoon. Expectations point to a no-change result on Wednesday, whereas investors generally anticipate a quarter-point hike in December . Strong wage growth momentum shown in the Labor Department's October payrolls report boosted the probability of a December rate hike .
Amazon Leads Advancing FANGs Amazon gained 2.5% to lead an early advance among FANG stocks , as well as Apple ( AAPL ) and Tesla ( TSLA ). The e-commerce giant announced it had expanded its Prime Now grocery delivery service from Whole Foods Markets to eight cities. It also announced a smart home security partnership with Schlage, a door and lock products unit of Allegion ( ALLE ).
Amazon is fighting to regain support at its 40-week moving average, and trading 20% off its September high.
Earnings News: Office Depot, Twilio, Planet Fitness In earnings news, Office Depot ( ODP ) soared 12%, and Groupon ( GRPN ) scrambled to a 2% gain after early reports. Infinera collapsed 32%, and medical products producer Innogen tumbled 2% after delivering reports late Tuesday.
Twilio vaulted 22% higher after reporting a third straight quarter of accelerating revenue growth . The early advance hinted at a move back above the stock's 50-day line and toward its old highs. The gap up gain put Twilio stock just below an 88.98 buy point. Until the market logs a follow-through day and returns to "confirmed uptrend" status , it is not a good time to purchase growth stocks.
Planet Fitness sprang ahead 14%, easily regaining support above its 50-day moving average. The budget-rate gym reported its strongest sales gain in four years , along with a third-quarter earnings beat and strong guidance. Shares are six weeks into a possible base pattern , with a potential buy point at 55.45.
Fashion leader Michael Kors ( KORS ) spilled 15% lower after reporting a mixed fiscal second-quarter performance . Shares are deep in a three-month correction.
Oil Prices Jump On OPEC Quota News Oil prices rose, possibly on news reports that the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries was set to discuss reducing its production quotas at a meeting scheduled over the coming weekend in Abu Dhabi.
Oil is looking to break a seven-day losing streak that has sent prices to their weakest level since March. West Texas Intermediate was up 0.7% in early trade, to just below $63 a barrel. Weekly production data is due out at 10:30 a.m. ET from the Energy Information Administration. A weekly report from the American Petroleum Institute late Tuesday said inventories rose for a fifth straight week.
Oil and gas producers reporting late Tuesday included Diamondback Energy ( FANG ), Energen ( EGN ), Devon Energy ( DVN ) and Cimarex ( XEC ).
